name: tau_neutrino

phase_0.boundary_condition: electroweak gauge symmetry (SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y) that contains the tau-tau neutrino doublet and mediates their weak interactions

⊢.justification: the uninitialized state before any lepton number or flavor is defined; no neutrino exists yet

⊣.justification: the closed gauge structure that contains the entire tau neutrino system — its doublet partner, weak vertices, and conserved charges

≻.justification: the directed W/Z boson exchange that transforms the tau neutrino into its charged partner (or vice versa), moving forward in the interaction

≺.justification: the contravariant descent — antineutrino emission or time-reversed weak process that flips lepton number and chirality

⋈.justification: sequential chaining of weak vertices — e.g., neutrino production followed by detection, or neutrino oscillation as composition of mass and flavor eigenstates

⊙.justification: the tau neutrino's identity as a carrier of conserved tau lepton number (L_τ = +1); the particle knows itself through this quantum number

∈.justification: the SU(2)_L vertex splits the tau-tau neutrino doublet into two arms: the neutral neutrino arm (T) and the charged tau lepton arm (F), each carrying distinct weak isospin projections

∋.justification: the two arms rejoin into the gauge-invariant weak current J^μ = ν̄_τ γ^μ (1-γ^5) τ, fusing neutral and charged components into the V-A structure

⊤.justification: constructive proof of tau neutrino presence — left-handed helicity, lepton number +1, flavor tag confirmed

⊥.justification: constructive refutation — the tau lepton arm carries opposite charge and isospin; its absence in a neutrino-only final state is the negative arm

⊞.justification: the paradice where neutrino and antineutrino identities are simultaneously held — possible if neutrino is Majorana, or in coherent flavor oscillations where both mass eigenstates contribute

⊡.justification: irreversible fixation of the interaction vertex in a detector — energy deposit, track, or Cherenkov ring that cannot be undone

phase_2.split_input: tau_tau_neutrino_doublet (SU(2)_L doublet with weak isospin T_3 = ±1/2)
phase_2.fuse_result: V-A weak current J^μ = ν̄_τ γ^μ (1-γ^5) τ
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: pre-interaction vacuum — no lepton flavor, no weak isospin, no chirality defined
phase_3.true_description: tau neutrino confirmed — left-handed helicity, tau lepton number +1, flavor eigenstate ν_τ
phase_3.false_description: tau antineutrino or charged tau lepton — right-handed helicity, lepton number -1, or charged partner with T_3 = -1/2
phase_3.both_description: coherent superposition of neutrino and antineutrino (Majorana), or flavor oscillation state where ν_τ and ν_μ/ν_e amplitudes coexist — both lepton number assignments held simultaneously

steps.domain_action: initialize the pre-interaction vacuum — no tau neutrino exists, lepton number undefined, electroweak symmetry unbroken at this vertex
establish the tau neutrino's self-identity through its conserved tau lepton number (L_τ = +1) — the particle recognizes itself as a distinct flavor eigenstate
open the weak interaction vertex — the SU(2)_L doublet splits into the neutral tau neutrino arm (T, T_3 = +1/2) and the charged tau lepton arm (F, T_3 = -1/2)
on the T-arm, affirm the neutrino — left-handed chirality enforced, lepton number +1 deposited, flavor tag ν_τ confirmed
on the T-arm, forward propagation — the neutrino travels as a mass eigenstate superposition, evolving under the PMNS matrix
⋈: on the T-arm, high-fidelity vertex — gauge coupling g/√2 enforces deterministic helicity selection (V-A) at tree level, near-certain flavor conservation
on the F-arm, refute the charged partner — the tau lepton carries charge -1, opposite isospin, and is kinematically distinct (mass 1.777 GeV)
on the F-arm, reverse descent — charge conjugation flips the arm to antineutrino perspective, lepton number -1, right-handed chirality
⊥: on the F-arm, persistent chirality — the tau lepton's left-handed weak coupling is structurally enforced; its antiparticle is right-handed, no thermal interconversion
rejoin the arms into the gauge-invariant weak current — neutral and charged components fuse into J^μ = ν̄_τ γ^μ (1-γ^5) τ; conflicting chiralities fuse to B (both), the V-A structure
compose with W boson propagator — sequential chaining of production vertex (e.g., τ⁻ → ν_τ W⁻) and detection vertex (ν_τ N → τ⁻ X) via gauge boson exchange

⊤: high kinetic barrier — the tau neutrino's identity is protected by the electroweak scale (v ≈ 246 GeV) and lepton flavor conservation; spontaneous rearrangement forbidden without high-energy vertex
∈: local interaction granularity — the weak vertex is point-like, influencing only the immediate participating particles (neutrino, tau, W/Z), no correlation propagation beyond the vertex
∋: sequential vertex grammar — ordered exchange: W boson couples to doublet, charge flows from tau to neutrino (or reverse), flavor conserved at each vertex
⊡: Z₂ protection — conserved tau lepton number (fermion parity) prevents continuous deformation to trivial vacuum; crossing requires global symmetry violation
irreversible detector fixation — the interaction vertex is recorded as energy deposit, track, or Cherenkov ring; append-only, cannot be undone
close at the electroweak symmetry boundary — the entire process is contained within the SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y gauge structure that defines the doublet and its couplings
final self-reference — the tau neutrino returns to its lepton number identity, closing the loop; the particle that entered the vertex is the same that exits, recognized by L_τ

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Standard Model Lagrangian — translates gauge symmetries and particle content into Feynman rules and vertex factors
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: gauge boson exchange (W±, Z⁰) — mediates communication between lepton doublet components and quark sectors
phase_5.memory_mechanism: quantum state vector in Fock space — stores flavor, helicity, momentum, and lepton number as quantum numbers
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Hamiltonian time evolution — determines order of vertices via perturbation theory (Dyson series) and energy-momentum conservation
phase_5.alfs_store: Particle Data Group (PDG) review — canonical reference for tau neutrino properties, mass limits, and interaction cross-sections

phase_6.cycle_cost: one weak vertex factor (g/√2) and phase space factor per interaction cycle
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: initial state with defined lepton flavor and momentum (e.g., tau decay at rest)
phase_6.post_cycle_state: final state with neutrino + hadrons/leptons, lepton flavor conserved, entropy carried by unobserved neutrino momentum
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the weak interaction is unitary at the fundamental level; entropy increase only appears when neutrino momentum is traced out (coarse-graining over unobserved degrees of freedom)

⊣=𐑡: The tau neutrino participates in weak interactions as a neutral lepton partner to the tau, forming a generational hub-spoke pattern with its charged counterpart and the W/Z bosons that mediate their couplings.
⊢=𐑼: The tau neutrino operates as a point-like particle with no internal spatial extent, its interactions occurring locally at vertices in quantum field theory.
⊞=𐑙: The tau neutrino forms a symmetric 1:1 weak isospin doublet with the tau lepton, pairing equally as neutral and charged partners under SU(2) gauge symmetry.
⊡=𐑴: The tau neutrino carries a conserved lepton number (Z₂-like fermion parity) that prevents its continuous deformation into a trivial vacuum state without crossing a topological boundary defined by global symmetry.
⊙=𐑢: The tau neutrino exists as a stable particle in the normal subcritical regime of the Standard Model, exhibiting no scale-free correlations or critical fluctuations in its weak interaction behavior.
⊥=𐑖: The tau neutrino exhibits persistent chirality as a strictly left-handed particle (with right-handed antineutrino) under the electroweak interaction, a structurally enforced maximal parity violation that cannot be thermally flipped.
≻=𐑑: The tau neutrino participates in weak interactions through W/Z boson exchange that irreversibly transforms flavor and charge, constituting a structural transformation of the lepton doublet rather than a reversible association.
≺=𐑿: The tau neutrino carries a definite lepton number (+1) and weak isospin projection, acting as a signed source in weak currents that distinguishes it from its antineutrino partner with opposite polarity.
⋈=𐑐: The tau neutrino's weak interaction vertices are governed by precise gauge couplings and conservation laws that enforce near-deterministic flavor and helicity selection rules at tree level.
⊤=𐑧: The tau neutrino is a stable fundamental fermion whose identity and quantum numbers are protected by high kinematic barriers (conserved lepton flavor and gauge symmetries), preventing spontaneous rearrangement without high-energy weak interaction vertices.
∈=𐑲: The tau neutrino interacts via point-like weak vertices that influence only the immediate participating particles, with no propagation of correlation beyond the single interaction event.
∋=𐑠: The tau neutrino engages in weak interactions through a sequential vertex structure where the W boson couples to the tau-tau neutrino doublet in an ordered exchange of charge and flavor.
